K-002929.check: rg prints existing constants or nothing; grep -c prints 2; grep -n for 200ms prints one line; grep -n for 8000ms prints one line.
traps: Small models show the skeleton immediately, which flickers on fast loads.
Write the thresholds in ms units to match the 200ms value.
Do not set the error timeout below 3000ms, since slow networks would fail early.

steps.do: Build the app for production.
Start the preview server on port 4173 in a second terminal.
Run axe against the tables route with WCAG 2 A and AA tags.
Print the exit code, where nonzero means violations remain.

K-002930.example: Running npx axe on http://localhost:4173/tables after the header fix prints no violation blocks and exits 0. If a td lacks a header association, axe prints the td-headers-attr rule with the selector and the run exits 1.
K-002930.check: axe prints no violation blocks, and echo prints 0.
traps: Scanning the dev server instead of the built preview can miss compiled markup.
Stopping at a passing scan without checking the exit code hides failures.
Axe only catches automatable issues, so keyboard and screen reader checks are still needed.

steps.do: Install dependencies from the lockfile.
Run svelte-check and treat any warning as a failure.
Confirm the summary line reports zero errors and zero warnings.
Confirm the table component declares a caption element.

K-002931.example: npx svelte-check --fail-on-warnings reports 0 errors and 0 warnings after adding an aria-label to an icon-only button. Removing the label brings back an a11y_ warning and the command exits 1.
K-002931.check: Output reads 'svelte-check found 0 errors and 0 warnings', the exit code is 0, and rg prints 1.
traps: svelte-check without --fail-on-warnings exits 0 even when warnings exist.
Compiler a11y warnings do not replace axe results, so run both.
Adding svelte-ignore comments to drop the warning count hides real defects.

steps.do: Install the Chromium browser for Playwright once.
Run the keyboard sort spec with the line reporter.
Confirm the spec presses keys at least twice, for Tab and Enter.
Confirm the spec asserts aria-sort changes from none to ascending after one Enter press.

K-002932.example: The spec tabs to the Name header button, presses Enter, and expects aria-sort ascending on the th within 200ms. A failure prints Expected 'ascending' Received 'none' on the sort header.
K-002932.check: The reporter prints '1 passed' and rg prints 2 or more.
traps: Playwright's click helper does not prove keyboard operability.
Asserting aria-sort only after a mouse click misses a missing Enter or Space handler.
Testing a stale build before Svelte recompiles can hide markup changes.

steps.do: Run the header scope spec against the tables route.
Count scope attributes in the component source to confirm the each block sets it.
Confirm the spec compares the header count to the number of data columns instead of a fixed number.

K-002933.example: The page has four columns, so the spec expects th[scope='col'] to count 4 after the Svelte each block renders. The source has one scope line inside the each block, which the DOM expands to four headers.
K-002933.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and rg prints 1.
traps: Counting source lines does not prove the runtime count, because each blocks expand.
Putting scope on td cells is wrong, since scope only applies to th headers.
Hardcoding the column count in the test breaks when columns are added.

steps.do: Build the production bundle.
Run axe with only the color-contrast rule on the light theme tables route.
Run the same rule on the dark theme route.
Print the exit code from the last run.

K-002934.example: Body text #595959 on #f5f5f5 measures 6.4:1 and passes, while zebra stripe text #aaaaaa on white measures 2.3:1 and fails. axe reports color-contrast on the striped td elements and exits 1.
K-002934.check: axe reports no color-contrast violations on either theme and echo prints 0.
traps: Checking only the default theme misses dark mode and striped row variants.
axe can skip elements with background images or opacity, so inspect those by hand.
Body table text needs 4.5:1, not the 3:1 that applies to large text.

steps.do: Print the dark-appearance text color values from the asset file.
Compute the contrast ratio of the dark text on the dark background with the checker script.
Confirm the script uses the 4.5 minimum for body text.
Lighten the text color if the printed ratio is below 4.5:1.

K-002935.example: The checker prints about 13.9:1 for #E8E8EA on #1C1C1E, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum. A pair printing 3.2:1 fails and the dark text value must be lightened.
K-002935.check: The script prints a ratio of 4.5 or higher, and grep shows the 4.5 threshold line.
traps: Small models pass the light-mode hex pair into a dark check, so use the dark appearance values.
Large text needs only 3:1, so do not apply that threshold to body copy.

steps.do: Search onboarding Swift files for fixed color literals.
Count lines that still hold fixed color literals. Expect 0.
Count named color references. Expect at least 1 per onboarding file.
Review each fixed-color match in context before replacing it with a named color from Assets.xcassets.

K-002936.example: A welcome title using .foregroundColor(.black) stays black on a dark background, so it becomes Color("TitleText") instead. After the fix, the first search returns no lines.
K-002936.check: The first rg prints nothing and exits 1, the fixed-literal count is 0, and the named-reference count is at least 1 for each onboarding file.
traps: Small models treat .white and .black as adaptive colors, but they are fixed values.
Search the whole Sources/Onboarding folder, not just one file.

steps.do: List onboarding files that define a SwiftUI preview.
Count dark-scheme preview declarations. Expect at least 1 per file from the previous step.
Count light-scheme preview declarations. Expect the same number as the dark count for each file.
List view files that have no dark preview. Expect no output.

K-002937.example: WelcomeView.swift has a #Preview using .preferredColorScheme(.dark) and another using .light. The rg counts for WelcomeView.swift show 1 for each, and the missing-dark search prints nothing.
K-002937.check: Every view file listed by the first search shows matching nonzero dark and light counts of at least 1, and the missing-dark search prints no lines.
traps: Small models add one preview and call it full coverage, but each view needs both schemes.
Setting @Environment(\.colorScheme) in a preview does not force the scheme; use .preferredColorScheme.

steps.do: List onboarding snapshot test files in the test target.
Count dark-mode test functions. Expect at least 1 per screen file.
Count light-mode test functions. Expect the same number as the dark count for each screen file.
List test files that have no dark-mode test. Expect no output.

K-002938.example: OnboardingWelcomeSnapshotTests has testWelcome_light and testWelcome_dark, so both counts are 1 for that file. A screen with only testWelcome fails the dark count and needs a second test.
K-002938.check: The find lists at least one file, each screen file shows equal nonzero light and dark counts of at least 1, and the missing-dark search prints no lines.
traps: Small models miss names like testWelcomeDark, so the pattern must match dark anywhere in the name.
A passing run does not prove dark coverage if no dark test exists.

steps.do: Confirm the contrast test file exists.
List the color pairs the test covers.
Run the contrast tests through the project target.
Confirm the test asserts the 4.5:1 minimum for body text.

K-002939.example: ContrastTests checks onboardingBody on surfaceWhite at 12.6:1 and onboardingCaption on surfaceWhite at 4.7:1. Both pairs pass the 4.5:1 minimum.
K-002939.check: make prints Test Suite OnboardingContrastTests passed, every pair is at or above 4.5:1, and the 4.5 grep returns at least one line.
traps: Small models apply the 3:1 large-text rule to body text, which needs 4.5:1.
Do not test one color pair and assume the rest pass.
Do not state a ratio by eye; the test must compute it.

steps.do: Count Button declarations in each onboarding file.
List every minHeight 44 modifier in onboarding views.
Confirm each Button has the 44pt frame on the button itself, or uses OnboardingButtonStyle.
Run the layout test that measures tap target sizes.

K-002940.example: The grep finds 4 Button declarations and 4 minHeight: 44 lines in OnboardingView.swift. The test prints All 4 targets at or above 44pt.
K-002940.check: The minHeight count is at least the Button count, and the test prints every target at or above 44pt with no failures.
traps: Small models put minHeight on a text view instead of the button.
Do not use 44 px; SwiftUI measures in points.
Do not raise padding alone, because the frame defines the hit area.

steps.do: Create the Sources/Select folder if it does not exist.
Create SelectViewModel.swift for the observable model.
Declare @Observable final class SelectViewModel with var query: String and a stored filtered array that refreshes in query's didSet.
In SelectView, hold the model with @State private var model = SelectViewModel(options: options) and render model.filtered in ForEach.
Search SelectView.swift for any filter calls, which should be none in the body.
Measure typing lag with 2,000 options in Instruments and confirm each keystroke stays under 16ms.

K-002941.example: Typing 'ger' into a 2,000-option country list runs refilter() once per keystroke instead of once per body pass. The grep for filter in SelectView.swift returns no lines.
K-002941.check: grep -n filter Sources/Select/SelectView.swift prints nothing, and the measured per-keystroke time is under 16ms.
traps: Putting .filter inside body reruns it on every state change.
Mutating options without refreshing filtered leaves stale results on screen.
Creating the model in body makes a new instance on every render, so use @State with an initializer that runs once.

steps.do: Locate the layout split that holds the chart area.
Build a Paragraph from the series values showing min, max and latest for each series.
Render the Paragraph into a Rect of at least 3 rows directly under the Chart.
Run the summary unit test that checks each line fits in 80 columns.

K-002942.example: The summary line reads 'cpu: min 12.0 max 98.5 last 40.2' and is 36 columns wide. The test chart_summary_lines_fit_80_columns passes.
K-002942.check: cargo test chart_summary prints 'test result: ok', and every summary line is 80 columns or fewer.
traps: Do not put the summary only in a tooltip or hidden panel, because readers then cannot reach it. Do not round values so much that min and max look the same.

steps.do: List the RGB values currently assigned to Dataset styles.
Add a function that computes WCAG relative luminance and the contrast ratio against Color::Rgb(0, 0, 0).
Write a test that asserts every series color has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
Run that test to prove every palette entry meets the threshold.

K-002943.example: Color::Rgb(0, 114, 178) gives about 4.05:1 on black and fails, so swap it for Color::Rgb(86, 180, 233) at about 9.1:1. The test wcag_contrast_palette_passes then prints ok.
K-002943.check: cargo test wcag_contrast prints 'test result: ok' and fails if Color::Rgb(0, 114, 178) is kept as a series color.
traps: The test must use the real terminal background, not always black, or the ratio is wrong. WCAG treats chart lines as non-text content with a 3:1 floor, so 4.5:1 is the stricter target chosen here.

steps.do: Search the source for any existing NO_COLOR handling before adding a new check.
Add a function that returns false when the NO_COLOR variable is set and not empty, using std::env::var_os.
In the Dataset builder, apply .style(Style::default().fg(color)) only when that function returns true, and otherwise leave the style at Style::default().
Run the named no-color test with NO_COLOR set to 1; the output must report exactly 1 passed and 0 failed.

K-002944.example: With NO_COLOR=1 set, color_enabled() returns false and every Dataset uses Style::default(). The output shows test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed for chart_no_color_has_no_fg.
K-002944.check: env NO_COLOR=1 cargo test chart_no_color_has_no_fg ends with 'test result: ok', and the summary line reads 1 passed; 0 failed.
traps: The NO_COLOR convention ignores an empty value, so check that the value is non-empty, not just that the variable exists. Setting NO_COLOR does not remove the Dataset markers, so keep them as the non-…

steps.do: List the Marker values already used in the chart module.
Assign Marker::Dot, Marker::Block and Marker::Braille to three different Datasets.
Set GraphType::Line on the first series and GraphType::Scatter on the second.
Run the uniqueness test; the output must report exactly 1 passed and 0 failed, which confirms the three series are distinct.

K-002945.example: cpu uses Marker::Braille with GraphType::Line, memory uses Marker::Dot with GraphType::Scatter, and disk uses Marker::Block with GraphType::Line. The output shows test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed.
K-002945.check: cargo test chart_series_have_unique_markers ends with 'test result: ok', and the summary line reads 1 passed; 0 failed.
traps: Two series with the same marker and the same GraphType look identical in monochrome, so vary at least one of them. Marker::Braille draws very small dots that some terminals render poorly, so do not u…

steps.do: Find the key handler that receives crossterm events for the chart view.
Map keys 1, 2 and 3 to toggle the visible flag of the matching series.
Render each series name with [on] or [off] in the legend title so the state is shown in text.
Run the digit-key test that presses 1 twice; the output must report exactly 1 passed and 0 failed.

K-002946.example: Pressing '1' changes cpu from [on] to [off] in the legend, and pressing it again restores [on]. The output shows test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed for toggle_series_with_digit_keys.
K-002946.check: cargo test toggle_series_with_digit_keys ends with 'test result: ok', and the summary line reads 1 passed; 0 failed.
traps: Do not show the hidden state only with color or a dimmed style, because some users cannot see that change. Check the digit keys with rg before adding them, so they do not conflict with existing bindi…

steps.do: Run a production build to get the baseline JS output.
List every JS chunk in dist/assets larger than 40 KB.
Write in PLAN.md that the modal chunk must stay under 30 KB gzip.
Re-run the build after the plan is written and confirm the total JS output still builds.

K-002947.example: The baseline shows index-a1b2.js at 210 KB, so the plan sets the modal chunk budget to 30 KB gzip. After the change, find should not list any Modal chunk over 30 KB.
K-002947.check: find prints no Modal chunk file over the budget, and the build exits with code 0.
traps: Measuring raw bytes instead of gzip gives a number that does not match the budget.
Setting the budget after the code is written turns it into a rubber stamp.

steps.do: Search the components for transform or filter rules that could trap fixed positioning.
Write in the plan that the Modal.vue root wraps its overlay in Teleport with to set to body.
Write a test that opens the modal and checks the overlay parent element is BODY.
Run the teleport test to confirm the overlay is a direct child of body.

K-002948.example: Modal.vue wraps its overlay in <Teleport to='body'> so an ancestor with transform: translateZ(0) cannot break position: fixed. The test checks that document.querySelector('.modal-overlay').parentElement.tagName equals BODY.
K-002948.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the overlay parent tag is BODY.
traps: Teleporting to a selector that does not exist logs a warning and renders nothing.
Teleport fixes layout problems, not slow modal content.
Server rendering needs the :disabled prop handled, or the overlay will not appear in the HTML.

steps.do: Find v-show uses in the modal template.
Plan to switch the heavy body from v-show to v-if so closed modals mount nothing.
Write a test that counts mounted .modal-body nodes while the modal is closed.
Run the mount test to confirm the count is 0 while closed.

K-002949.example: A modal with a 300-field form under v-show mounts 300 inputs at page load, but under v-if it mounts none until opened. The test expects document.querySelectorAll('.modal-body').length to equal 0 before the open click.
K-002949.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the mounted body count is 0 while the modal is closed.
traps: v-if remounts the body on every open, so an expensive first render repeats each time.
Keep v-show for cheap toggles such as a tooltip.
Check the count with the modal closed, not after it opens.

steps.do: Record in the plan a budget of 200 ms from click to visible dialog.
Write a Playwright test that clicks the open button and times until the role dialog is visible.
Run the timing test against the production preview build.
Run a Lighthouse performance audit on the preview page that hosts the modal.

K-002950.example: The test clicks #open-modal and expects the elapsed time to be under 200 ms, failing with a message like 'expected 340 to be less than 200' when it is slower. The Lighthouse run must report a performance score of at least 90.
K-002950.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and Lighthouse reports a performance score of 0.90 or higher.
traps: Timing the Vite dev server gives numbers much slower than production, so use the preview build.
Start the clock at the click event, and wait for the transition to end before reading the time.

steps.do: Count addEventListener lines in the modal component file.
Count removeEventListener lines in the same file.
Plan to add listeners in onMounted and remove the same function references in onBeforeUnmount.
Run the leak test that opens and closes the modal 50 times and checks the listener count.

K-002951.example: Modal.vue adds keydown and focusin listeners in onMounted, so rg -c prints 2 for addEventListener and nothing for removeEventListener before the plan is applied. After the plan, both counts must be 2 and the leak test must report a listener delta of 0.
K-002951.check: Both rg counts match, and Playwright prints '1 passed' with a listener delta of 0.
traps: rg -c counts matching lines, not calls, so one line can hide several listeners.
An anonymous arrow function passed to addEventListener cannot be removed, so store the handler in a named const.

steps.do: Find every static import of the modal component in src.
Record the entry chunk size in bytes before the change.
Replace each static import with defineAsyncComponent wrapping a literal dynamic import of Modal.vue.
Rebuild the app so the new split takes effect.
Confirm no static import of the modal remains in src.
Measure the entry chunk size in bytes after the rebuild and compare it with the recorded value.

K-002952.example: src/App.vue has import Modal from './components/Modal.vue' today, and the plan replaces it with const Modal = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('./components/Modal.vue')). Before the change the entry chunk is 184320 bytes. After npm run build it is 151040 bytes, which is 33280 bytes smaller. Then rg -n 'import .*Modal' src prints nothing.
K-002952.check: The second rg run prints no lines and exits with code 1. The entry chunk size after the rebuild is at least 10000 bytes smaller than the size recorded before the change.
traps: defineAsyncComponent does not preload, so the first open waits for the network.
A dynamic import() with a path built at runtime prevents Vite from splitting the chunk.
Wrapping the modal in v-if does not remove it from the entry chunk.

steps.do: Build the nav stylesheet from the input file with minification.
Read the byte count of the built file.
Record the budget of 4096 bytes in plans/nav-css-budget.md.
If the count is over 4096, list the nav utility classes and cut any used only once.
Rebuild the stylesheet and read the byte count again.

K-002953.example: The nav build writes dist/nav.css at 3150 bytes, which is under the 4096 budget, so the plan keeps it inline. stat -c %s prints 3150.
K-002953.check: The final stat -c %s prints a number below 4096.
traps: Do not measure the unminified file, because whitespace inflates the count and gives a false result.
Do not measure the whole app stylesheet. Measure only the nav build so the number reflects the nav.

steps.do: Start the local dev server in a separate terminal and note the port it prints.
Record a Lighthouse performance baseline for the home page as JSON.
Read the performance score from the JSON file.
Write the target as a performance score of at least 0.90 and LCP under 2500ms.
Confirm the baseline file exists and is not empty.

K-002954.example: The baseline run prints 0.72 for the home page, so the plan targets 0.90 and LCP under 2500ms. jq reads 0.72 from plans/baseline.json.
K-002954.check: jq prints a number between 0 and 1, and wc -c prints a count above zero.
traps: Do not compare a dev server run with a production build, because their numbers are not comparable.
Do not record the baseline before the nav is in place, or the score will not reflect the nav at all.

steps.do: List where the desktop-first pattern already appears so the plan can change it.
Create the plans folder.
Create the plan file, then write base classes for below 768px and md: classes that add the desktop layout.
Count the md: toggles in the plan. The count must be 3 or fewer.
Confirm the plan file exists.

K-002955.example: The nav has 6 links, and 4 of them use hidden md:flex, so the plan keeps a 2-link base row and reveals the rest at md. rg -c -F "md:" plans/nav-breakpoints.md prints 2 for that plan.
K-002955.check: rg -n -F prints the current desktop-first lines, rg -c prints a number no greater than 3, and test -f plans/nav-breakpoints.md exits 0.
traps: Do not write desktop-first classes like flex md:hidden, because mobile then downloads the wider layout first. Keep the base classes mobile and add md: on top.
Do not guess the count of hidden links, because the rg count is the only reliable number.

steps.do: Find fixed positioning in the nav so it can change to sticky top-0 on the wrapper, which keeps the page's space.
Find the current transition and duration classes so they can be limited to transform and opacity with duration-200.
Find existing reduced-motion classes and add motion-reduce:transition-none where they are missing.
Find nav elements that use transition-all, since it animates layout properties too.
Find any transition of 300ms or longer in the source.
Count the duration-200 classes in the nav file, which must be at least 1.

K-002956.example: The header uses sticky top-0 with transition-[transform,opacity] duration-200. rg -c -F "duration-200" src/Nav.tsx prints 1 after the plan is applied.
K-002956.check: rg -n -F transition-all src and rg -n -e "duration-[3-9]" src print no lines once the plan is applied, and rg -c -F "duration-200" src/Nav.tsx prints at least 1.
traps: Do not use transition-all, because it animates width and height and causes layout work on every frame.
Do not switch to fixed without adding a spacer, because the page content then jumps up under the header.

steps.do: Install the Chromium browser for Playwright once.
Open tests/drawer-motion.spec.ts and confirm it finds the dialog element with getByRole.
Run the drawer motion test.
Confirm the test reads the animation duration from document.getAnimations and asserts at most 300 milliseconds.
Rerun with tracing on to inspect timing if the test fails.

K-002957.example: Drawer.tsx sets transition transform 240ms ease-out, so the spec asserts a measured duration of 240 ms. A measured duration of 480 ms means the timing doubled and the test fails.
K-002957.check: Playwright prints 1 passed and the logged duration is 240 ms or less.
traps: Small models often wait with a fixed sleep instead of waiting for the animation to finish.
Checking only opacity while ignoring transform gives a false pass.
Do not raise the 300 millisecond limit to make the test green.

steps.do: Check the layout folder declares a prefers-reduced-motion media query.
Run the reduced-motion Playwright tests.
Open the spec and confirm it calls page.emulateMedia with reducedMotion set to reduce.
Run the unit test that mocks matchMedia.

K-002958.example: The spec sets reducedMotion to reduce, then reads getComputedStyle on the .drawer element. The transitionDuration must be 0s, and a value of 0.24s fails the test.
K-002958.check: rg prints a line such as src/layout/Drawer.module.css:12 with the media query, and Playwright prints 1 passed.
traps: Small models add the media query in CSS but leave a JavaScript animation running.
Checking only the stylesheet misses inline style transitions.
Do not hard code matchMedia to false in the tests.

steps.do: Build the production bundle.
Serve the built app on port 4173.
Run Lighthouse on the layout route and save the results as JSON.
Read the cumulative-layout-shift numeric value from the report.
Confirm the printed value is below 0.1.

K-002959.example: The /layout route reports a cumulative-layout-shift numericValue of 0.02 after the drawer switches to transform. A value of 0.25 means the accordion height animation pushes content down.
K-002959.check: jq prints a number such as 0.02 that is less than 0.1.
traps: Small models measure the dev server instead of the production build, which inflates the score.
Do not report CLS from a single Lighthouse run.
A missing JSON file means the run failed, not that the score passed.

steps.do: Check the Collapse component uses useLayoutEffect for measurement.
Run the Collapse unit test.
Confirm the test mocks scrollHeight as 240 on the content element.
Run TypeScript to confirm the ref type matches HTMLDivElement.

K-002960.example: Collapse.tsx reads contentRef.current.scrollHeight inside useLayoutEffect and writes the custom property --collapse-height as 240px before paint. The test checks that --collapse-height equals 240px after the panel opens.
K-002960.check: rg prints a line containing useLayoutEffect, Vitest prints 1 passed, and tsc prints nothing.
traps: Small models switch to useEffect, which paints one frame late and flashes zero height.
They also test the animation end without asserting the measured height.
Do not mock useLayoutEffect away.

steps.do: Confirm the spec calls requestAnimationFrame in a loop for 450 milliseconds.
Run the frame-counter test.
Run the same test on the chromium project to check the browser used.
Compare the logged frame count against 27 frames.

K-002961.example: Playwright starts the Sheet open transition, counts requestAnimationFrame ticks over 450 ms, and logs frames=28. A logged frames=14 means the animation ran near 30fps, so the test fails.
K-002961.check: The log shows frames=27 or higher and Playwright prints 1 passed.
traps: Small models start counting before the animation begins, so the count runs low.
Headless browsers can throttle requestAnimationFrame, so check which project ran.
Do not lower the 27 frame threshold to make a failing run pass.

steps.do: List the CSS module files in the layout folder.
Search for transitions that name width, height, top, or left.
Print each transition declaration and read its duration. Flag any duration above 200ms.
Fail the review if step 2 printed any line. Run the search quietly and read the exit status: 0 means a layout-property transition exists, 1 means none.

K-002962.example: Sidebar.module.css transitions only transform and opacity, so step 2 prints no lines and step 4 exits with status 1. Accordion.module.css with a height transition of 300ms prints one line in step 2, exits with status 0 in step 4, and must switch to a scaleY transform.
K-002962.check: Step 4 exits with status 1, which means zero layout property transitions. Step 3 lists every transition duration, and none exceeds 200ms.
traps: Small models flag any width declaration as an animation even when it is static layout.
Only lines with transition or animation count toward the check.
Do not accept an animation on top or left because the change looks small.

steps.do: List every media query in the source tree.
Confirm the Vue version from package.json.
Count the distinct min-width values that the toast layout must respond to.
Create PLAN.md to hold the breakpoint list as the single source for toast layout.
Record that toasts go full width below 640px and use a 24rem card from 1024px.

K-002963.example: The app uses 640px and 1024px breakpoints, so the plan sets the toast container to full width below 640px and a 24rem card from 1024px. The grep prints 'vue': '^3.4.21', which confirms that Composition API and script setup are available.
K-002963.check: rg prints at least one @media line per breakpoint, and grep prints a line with the vue version such as ^3.4.21.
traps: A small model often invents breakpoints instead of reading them from the code.
It also skips the Vue major version check, so it may use Vue 2 APIs such as Vue.extend.

steps.do: Search the source for the 320px smallest supported width.
Set the maximum visible toasts to 3 and write it in the plan.
Set the toast width to min(100vw - 2rem, 24rem) so it fits 320px screens.
Find the root font size in CSS to convert 2rem and 24rem to pixels.
Confirm the 320px viewport leaves a 16px gutter on each side.

K-002964.example: At 320px the toast is min(100vw - 2rem, 24rem), which is 288px wide with 16px margins on each side. With a 16px root size, 2rem is 32px of total gutter.
K-002964.check: rg prints the 320px lines it finds, and the planned width at 320px is 288px, which is 320 minus 32.
traps: A small model may set a fixed 400px width that overflows 320px screens.
It also confuses rem with px, so the gutter is wrong when the root font size changes.

steps.do: Search for existing env safe-area usage in the stylesheets.
Confirm the viewport meta tag includes viewport-fit=cover in index.html.
Plan the bottom offset as max(1rem, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) and record it in PLAN.md.
Plan the close button as at least 44px by 44px for touch.
Count the close-button matches in the components to check each has the 44px target.

K-002965.example: The meta line becomes content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover' so env(safe-area-inset-bottom) returns a real value on iPhone. The close button is 44px by 44px, which meets the 44px target size.
K-002965.check: grep prints a viewport line that contains viewport-fit=cover, and rg -c prints a count of close-button matches in src/components.
traps: A small model may forget viewport-fit=cover, so env() returns 0 and notch overlap goes unnoticed.
It may also plan a 24px close button, which fails the 44px target.

steps.do: Search for existing transition classes and durations in the styles.
Set the enter and leave duration to 200ms and record it in PLAN.md.
Search for an existing prefers-reduced-motion rule to reuse.
Confirm the installed Vue major version supports TransitionGroup.
Set the auto-dismiss timer to 5000ms for toasts with an action and 3000ms otherwise.

K-002966.example: The plan sets enter and leave to 200ms, with a prefers-reduced-motion block that sets 0ms. grep returns 'vue': '^3.4.21', which supports TransitionGroup with the name prop.
K-002966.check: rg prints the existing transition lines, and grep prints a Vue 3 version line such as ^3.4.21.
traps: A small model may set the reduced-motion duration to a value other than 0ms, which still animates for users who asked for less motion.
It may also set the auto-dismiss timer without a 5000ms case for toasts that have an action button.

steps.do: Search for existing matchMedia calls that a toast could reuse.
Check whether @vueuse/core is installed for useMediaQuery.
Create PLAN.md to hold the decision that position and size stay in CSS and JavaScript only handles behavior.
List the toast position rules in the stylesheet directory.
Check that the toast breakpoint is 639px in the stylesheet.
Confirm the reduced-motion query is the only JavaScript media check.

K-002967.example: If grep finds @vueuse/core at ^10.9.0, the plan can use useMediaQuery('(max-width: 639px)') for the one behavior that needs JavaScript. Position stays in CSS so the toast does not jump on first paint.
K-002967.check: rg prints zero or more matchMedia lines; grep prints a vueuse version line if the package is installed, and prints nothing with exit code 1 if it is not; rg -n 639px prints one line per stylesheet that sets the breakpoint, and it must match 639px exactly.
traps: Small models often wrap every layout rule in a JavaScript ref, which causes flicker on first render.
useMediaQuery returns false until it runs on the client, so do not use it for initial placement.

steps.do: List the two panel states as visible and hidden, using the hidden attribute on each role=tabpanel element.
Find the stylesheets to edit, excluding node_modules.
Create a PLAN.md file to record the planned fade duration of 200ms with ease-out.
Count the prefers-reduced-motion guards that already exist in the stylesheet.
Check that the planned 200ms duration appears in the plan file.

K-002972.check: The grep -c command prints 1 or more, and the PLAN.md grep prints one line containing 200ms.

Animating display directly does not transition without allow-discrete. Plan opacity and transform for the fade instead.

steps.do: Write the 300ms maximum for one tab switch into PLAN.md as the single number to enforce.
Confirm the Playwright config file exists.
List the planned Playwright tests without running them to count the cases.
Check that the 300ms budget appears in the plan file.
Decide that the test asserts the new panel is visible within 300ms of the click.

K-002973.check: The npx playwright test --list output ends with Total: 2 tests in 1 file, and the grep prints a line containing 300ms.
traps: The --list flag does not run the tests, so a listed test is not a passing test. Run the suite in the build or verify stage.
The 300ms figure is a maximum, not a target. Do not plan the animation to use all of it.
The listing fails if the config file is missing. Confirm the config with test -f first.

steps.do: List the panel elements that use the hidden attribute in the markup.
Check whether the stylesheet already declares allow-discrete for display changes.
Confirm the stylesheet file exists before any edit.
List the project files to confirm the page directory is the expected one.
Plan the fade-out as 200ms of opacity before display changes to none.

K-002974.example: The markup shows 3 hidden panels, and the plan sets transition-behavior to allow-discrete so the 200ms fade ends with display none. Before the build, the allow-discrete count prints 0.
K-002974.check: The rg -n command lists 3 lines containing hidden, and the allow-discrete count prints 0 before the build stage.

The allow-discrete keyword must appear in the transition list too, or the display change does not wait for the fade.
Setting display none immediately skips the fade entirely. Plan the opacity change first.

steps.do: List every colour value used in the form's stylesheet.
Save a script at tools/contrast.py that computes the WCAG contrast ratio for a foreground and background pair.
Run the contrast script on the palette file so every pair gets a ratio.
Mark each text pair under 4.5:1 and each focus-indicator pair under 3:1 as failing in the plan.
Replace each failing colour in the plan with the nearest pair that passes.

K-002975.example: The pair #767676 text on #ffffff gives about 4.54:1, so it passes the 4.5:1 text rule. The focus border #aaaaaa on #ffffff gives about 2.3:1, which fails the 3:1 focus rule.
K-002975.check: tools/contrast.py prints every pair with its ratio, every text pair shows 4.5 or higher, and every focus pair shows 3 or higher.
traps: Contrast must be measured on the actual rendered pair, not on the colour named in a design file. The user's terminal theme can remap colours, so a fixed hex value is only a plan target. Focus indicat…

steps.do: Confirm useTheme.js exists under src/composables.
Run the Vitest spec that covers toggle, initial value, and persistence.
Check that the spec asserts the localStorage key named theme.
Type-check the composable's JSDoc types without emitting files.

K-002976.example: After toggle() moves the theme from light to dark, document.documentElement.dataset.theme and localStorage.theme both read dark. The spec reports 4 passing tests, and tsc prints nothing.
K-002976.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 4 passed (4)', grep prints at least one line with localStorage, and tsc exits 0 with no output.
traps: Small models often test the ref value but not the data-theme attribute on document.documentElement. Assert both.
Do not mock localStorage with a plain object that skips the string conversion. Assert the stored value is the string dark.
Vitest runs in jsdom, which has no matchMedia by default. Stub window.matchMedia in the spec or the composable throws.

steps.do: Confirm the e2e spec file exists.
Run the dark-mode contrast test in Chromium only.
List the tests in the file to count the dark-mode cases.

K-002977.example: The spec sets the page to dark, reads the computed color and background of each nav link, and asserts a ratio of at least 4.5:1. The run reports 1 passed for the dark-mode test.
K-002977.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' with no failed tests, and the --list output names the dark-mode test.
traps: Small models read the color of the wrapper div, not the link text. Measure the element that holds the text.
The text is 16px or larger and not bold for AA body text, so the threshold is 4.5:1, not 3:1. Use 4.5:1 unless the spec says otherwise.
Playwright must set the color scheme before the page loads. Use the colorScheme option in the test, not a click after load.

steps.do: Build the production bundle so the scan runs on the real output.
Serve the built app on port 4173 in the background.
Run the axe accessibility spec that loops over light and dark themes.
Count the axe spec cases to confirm both themes are covered.

K-002978.example: The spec opens the app with the light theme, runs axe with the wcag2aa tag, then repeats with the dark theme. Each run reports zero violations for the nav landmark.
K-002978.check: Playwright prints '2 passed', and grep prints a count of 2 or more.
traps: A dark-mode-only scan misses light-mode failures. Scan both themes every time.
Axe checks computed styles, so a theme class must be applied before the scan starts. Wait for the attribute to change.
Do not treat zero axe violations as proof of contrast. Axe can report incomplete results, so check that the incomplete count is also reported.

steps.do: Create the reports directory for the Lighthouse output.
Run Lighthouse accessibility only against the preview server, with dark mode forced by the page query.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report.

K-002979.example: Lighthouse writes the report to reports/lh-nav-dark.json while the preview server serves the app in dark mode. The jq command prints 0.97 for the accessibility score.
K-002979.check: jq prints a number of 0.95 or higher, and the file reports/lh-nav-dark.json exists.
traps: Lighthouse scores the whole page, not only the nav. Check the nav-specific audit IDs in the report if the score is low.
The query parameter theme=dark only works if the app reads it. Confirm the app reads it before trusting the run.
Lighthouse needs a built app served over HTTP, not the Vite dev server with hot reload running. Use the preview port.

steps.do: Find the line in index.html where the theme attribute is set by an inline script.
Confirm that line sits inside the head, which is within the first 15 lines of the file.
Run the flash spec that compares the theme at DOMContentLoaded with the first paint.

K-002980.example: The inline script in index.html line 8 sets data-theme before the body renders. The flash spec reads the attribute at first paint and sees dark with no change afterward.
K-002980.check: grep prints a line number of 15 or less, head shows the script in the head section, and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: A script placed at the bottom of body runs after first paint, so the nav flashes. Move it into the head.
Small models set the attribute in onMounted, which is too late for the first paint. Use a blocking inline script.
Checking only the final state misses the flash. The spec must record the attribute at first paint, not after load.

steps.do: Search AppNav.vue for hex or rgb color literals.
Count how many color values come from theme variables.
Lint the component file with the Vue ESLint rules.

K-002981.example: The first grep finds no matches, and the second finds 6 lines that use var(--nav-text) or var(--nav-bg). ESLint exits with no errors on AppNav.vue.
K-002981.check: The first grep prints nothing and exits 1, the count is 6 or more, and eslint prints no problems.
traps: Small models forget that a color can be set in a style attribute, so search the template too, not only the style block.
grep exit code 1 means no match, which is the pass case here. Do not treat it as a tool failure.
A variable name must match the one defined in theme.css. Check the names exist with grep before trusting the count.

steps.do: Create index.html with a lang attribute on the html element and a viewport meta tag in the head.
Wrap the page in a header element, a nav element, one main element, and a footer element.
Give each nav its own aria-label when the page has more than one nav.
Count the main opening tags to confirm there is exactly one.
Run axe against the served page with WCAG 2 A and AA rules and fail on any violation.

K-002982.example: A page has a header, a nav with aria-label Primary, one main with id main, and a footer. The rg count prints 1 and axe exits with status 0.
K-002982.check: rg prints 1 and the axe command exits with status 0 with no violations listed.
traps: Using a div with class main instead of a real main element removes the landmark for screen readers.
Adding two main elements or a nav without a label makes landmarks ambiguous.
Skipping the lang attribute makes screen readers pick the wrong pronunciation.

steps.do: Add an anchor with class skip-link and href set to #main as the first child of body.
Set id main and tabindex -1 on the main element so focus moves into the content.
Hide the skip link off screen with transform translateY(-200%) instead of display none.
Under the selector .skip-link:focus, set transform to none and give it a background with at least 4.5:1 contrast against its text.
Confirm the class is in the stylesheet.
Run a Playwright test that presses Tab once and checks the link is visible with a bounding box height above 0.

K-002983.example: The first Tab press focuses a link reading Skip to main content at the top left of the page, and pressing Enter moves focus to main. The rg command prints the line number of the .skip-link rule in styles.css.
K-002983.check: rg prints at least one line number and Playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: Using display none hides the link from keyboard users too, so it can never be focused.
Forgetting the id on main means the href points nowhere.
Placing the link after the header defeats its purpose because the header is already tabbed through.

steps.do: Write the markup in reading order: header, nav, main, aside, footer.
Define grid-template-areas on the .layout selector and give each child a grid-area name that matches.
Check the stylesheet for any order property, which changes visual order without changing DOM order.
Run a Playwright test that reads all landmark elements in DOM order and compares them to the expected list.

K-002984.example: Markup lists header, main, and aside in that order, and on wide screens the grid places aside on the right of main with grid-area aside. The grep count prints 0 because no order property is used.
K-002984.check: grep prints 0 and Playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: Using the CSS order property moves items visually but screen readers still read the DOM order, so the two disagree.
Writing grid-area names that do not match the grid-template-areas strings leaves items unplaced.
Matching the word border with a looser pattern makes a grep count wrong.

steps.do: Add a rule for :focus-visible that sets outline to 3px solid #1a4fd6 with outline-offset 2px.
Check that the outline color has at least 3:1 contrast against the adjacent background, which #1a4fd6 on #ffffff gives about 6.6:1.
Search the stylesheet for any outline none rule that would remove focus.
Run a Playwright test that tabs to each focusable panel and checks the computed outline width is at least 2px.

K-002985.example: A card with tabindex 0 shows a 3px blue outline with a 2px gap when focused by keyboard. The grep command prints nothing and exits with status 1, meaning no outline none rule exists.
K-002985.check: grep prints no lines and Playwright reports 1 passed with computed outline width of 3px or more.
traps: Setting outline none without a replacement hides focus from keyboard users completely.
Using a pale outline color under 3:1 contrast fails the non-text contrast rule.
Relying on :focus instead of :focus-visible shows the ring after mouse clicks, which can look wrong, though it still passes.

steps.do: Set the nav a selector to display inline-flex, min-height 44px, and min-width 44px.
Use padding of 0.5rem 0.75rem so the text stays inside the 44px box with the root font size of 16px.
Confirm the 44px value is present in the stylesheet.
Run a Playwright test that reads each nav link boundingBox and expects width and height of at least 44.

K-002986.example: Each nav link is an inline-flex box at least 44px tall and wide, with padding 0.5rem 0.75rem. The rg command prints the line where min-height 44px is set.
K-002986.check: rg prints at least one matching line and Playwright reports 1 passed with every link at least 44px in both dimensions.
traps: Padding on a plain inline element does not enlarge its clickable box, so use inline-flex or inline-block.
Writing 44 without the px unit or with a different unit makes the rule invalid or wrong.
Checking only the height and not the width misses narrow links.

steps.do: Set the layout grid to grid-template-columns minmax(0, 1fr) for narrow screens and make img elements max-width 100%.
Search the stylesheet for minmax to confirm the safe column definition is present.
Run a Playwright test with a viewport of 320 by 568 pixels that expects document scrollWidth to be at most 320.
Run Lighthouse for accessibility only and save the report as JSON.
Read the accessibility score from the report.

K-002987.example: At 320px width the scrollWidth measures 320 and the grid uses one column. The jq command prints 0.96, which is above the 0.9 threshold.
K-002987.check: grep prints the minmax line, Playwright reports 1 passed, and jq prints a number of 0.9 or higher.
traps: Using a plain 1fr column lets long text or images force the column wider than the viewport.
Fixed pixel widths on containers cause horizontal scrolling at 320px.
Forgetting the viewport meta tag makes mobile browsers ignore the narrow layout and test the wrong width.

steps.do: Create the input source folder.
Create the search view file.
In SearchField.swift, declare @State private var query = "" and a List over results, with the filter function defined outside body.
Attach .task(id: query) and inside it call try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 250_000_000) before filtering, so only the last keystroke runs the filter.
Confirm the 250ms sleep appears exactly once in the file.

K-002988.example: The user types 'swi' quickly, and only one filter runs after 250ms of quiet. Each new keystroke cancels the previous task automatically because .task(id:) restarts when query changes.
K-002988.check: rg prints 1 for SearchField.swift, and no filter call appears in the body of the view.
traps: Calling a filter directly in body reruns it on every render. Using onChange with a new Task per keystroke leaves stale results without cancellation. Omitting Task.sleep gives no debounce at all.

steps.do: Add the unicode-width crate to the project.
In src/input.rs write fn fit_width that takes s and max_cols, adds each char's width with UnicodeWidthChar::width, and stops before the first char that would exceed max_cols.
Add a test named fit_width_never_splits_wide that asserts fit_width of 日本語テキスト with 5 columns returns 日本.
Run the fit_width tests to check the boundary behavior.

K-002989.example: fit_width of 日本語テキスト with max 5 returns 日本 with width 4, because adding 語 would make the width 6. The result leaves one column blank, which is correct.
K-002989.check: cargo test fit_width prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed' and the assertion for 日本 passes.
traps: Using s.chars().take(max_cols) can exceed the field width by up to double for wide characters.
Stopping at max_cols without checking the next char's width can leave half a glyph on screen.
Counting every char as width 1 ignores zero-width marks that should add nothing.

steps.do: Start the dev server that serves the onboarding page.
Create a Playwright spec that reads getComputedStyle font-size and line-height of the onboarding h1 and p elements.
Run the onboarding typography spec.
Confirm the h1 computes to 36px font-size and 40px line-height, which is Tailwind text-4xl at the default theme.
Confirm the body paragraph computes to at least 16px, which is 1rem.

K-002990.example: The h1 with class text-4xl must compute to font-size 36px and line-height 40px. The body paragraph with class text-base must compute to 16px, or 1rem at the root size.
K-002990.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the spec asserts the h1 computed font-size equals 36px and line-height equals 40px.
traps: Checking only the class name in the JSX, which says nothing about the computed size if the theme was overridden.
Assuming text-4xl is 36px in every project, when an @theme block may have changed --text-4xl.
Forgetting that line-height comes with the text-4xl pairing, so the 40px line-height must be asserted too.

steps.do: Find the @theme block in the global stylesheet to confirm the token is declared there.
Build the Tailwind v4 stylesheet to dist/app.css.
Check the built CSS contains the brand-600 custom property with its hex value.
Confirm the match prints the exact token name and hex value.

K-002991.example: In src/styles/app.css, @theme declares --color-brand-600: #2563eb, which makes the class bg-brand-600 available. After the build, grep prints --color-brand-600: #2563eb.
K-002991.check: The grep prints one line, '--color-brand-600: #2563eb', and the rg step shows the @theme line in app.css.
traps: Using the v3 tailwind.config.js colors key, which is not how v4 declares tokens.
Writing the token as --color-brand-600 but using a class like bg-brand600 without the hyphen, so the utility never generates.
Trusting the source file alone, since a token only ships if the build generates the utility that uses it.

steps.do: Start the dev server serving the onboarding route.
List each text color token and its background token used on the onboarding screens, with the hex values.
Run axe with WCAG 2.0 AA tags against the onboarding page.
Confirm axe exits with code 0 and lists no color-contrast violation.
Compute by hand any pair you are unsure of, requiring at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

K-002992.example: text-slate-500 (#64748b) on white is about 4.76:1 and passes the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold. text-slate-400 (#94a3b8) on white is about 2.57:1 and fails, so it must not hold onboarding body copy.
K-002992.check: axe exits 0 with no color-contrast entry, and each listed text pair is at least 4.5:1 unless it is large text.
traps: Checking only the primary text while the muted helper text uses a lighter token that fails.
Treating 3:1 as the normal-text threshold, which applies only to large text.
Assuming dark mode tokens pass because the light mode pair did.

steps.do: Confirm the spacing token stepGap exists and is a non-null value in the token file.
Confirm the font sans token exists and is a non-null value in the same file.
Confirm the stepGap value is 1.5rem, which is 24px at a 16px root.
Confirm the Tailwind stylesheet maps the font token to --font-sans in @theme.

K-002993.example: tokens/onboarding.json has spacing.stepGap set to 1.5rem, so jq -e prints 1.5rem and exits 0. The font.sans value must be a string such as Inter, and app.css must map it to --font-sans in @theme.
K-002993.check: Each jq -e prints a non-null value and exits 0, and rg prints the --font-sans line in app.css.

steps.do: Start the dev server serving the onboarding route.
Create the reports directory for the audit output.
Run Lighthouse accessibility only and save the JSON report.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report, which must be at least 0.9.
Confirm the target-size audit score is 1 and that onboarding buttons use h-11 or min-h-11, which is 2.75rem or 44px.

K-002994.example: A primary button with class h-11 px-6 computes to 44px tall, which meets the 44px target. Lighthouse then reports a target-size score of 1 and an accessibility score of 0.96 or higher.
K-002994.check: The jq score prints 0.9 or above for accessibility, and the target-size score prints 1 with the 44px button heights confirmed.
traps: Using h-10, which is 2.5rem or 40px and falls short of the 44px target.
Trusting the overall accessibility score without reading the target-size audit itself.
Comparing numbers from a dev server run with numbers from a production build.

steps.do: Search the onboarding components for arbitrary font-size brackets.
Search the onboarding components for arbitrary leading brackets.
Search the onboarding components for arbitrary tracking brackets.
Replace each hit with a scale class such as text-sm or leading-6, or add a named --text-* token in @theme. Rerun the three searches until each prints no lines and exits with code 1.
Run the onboarding typography spec, which reads each computed font-size and line-height in the browser and fails if any value is outside the token set or below 16px for body text.

K-002995.example: Step.tsx line 42 contains class text-[1.1rem], which should become a named token. After adding --text-lede: 1.1rem in @theme, the class becomes text-lede. The searches then print nothing, and the Playwright run reports 'passed' with 0 failures, where the spec's computed-size check confirms the rendered value matches the token.
K-002995.check: npx playwright test exits 0 and reports 0 failed tests, and the three rg searches print nothing and exit 1.
traps: Searching only text-[ and missing arbitrary leading-[ or tracking-[ values.
Replacing an arbitrary value with a raw pixel number in style=, which bypasses tokens entirely; the Playwright spec catches this because it checks computed styles, not class names.
Treating an empty rg search as proof the page is correct, when only the Playwright run measures the rendered font-size and line-height.
Leaving a non-empty hit in place and assuming it is fine because the page renders.

steps.do: Choose error text color #b00020 on a #ffffff background, which measures 7.3:1.
Start a local static server on port 8000 for the page.
Run axe against the page and check for color-contrast violations.
Confirm the chosen hex value appears in styles.css.
Record the minimum ratio 4.5:1 for text under 24px in PLAN.md.

K-002996.example: The error toast uses color #b00020 on #ffffff at 7.3:1, above the 4.5:1 threshold. The axe run reports 0 color-contrast violations for the toast.
K-002996.check: npx axe prints 0 violations for color-contrast, and grep prints a line like 'color: #b00020;' from styles.css.
traps: Small models estimate contrast by eye instead of measuring it.

steps.do: Count buttons already on the page so the close button does not clash with them.
Decide the container uses position fixed, inset-block-end 1rem, and inset-inline-end 1rem.
Decide the close button has min-width and min-height of 44px.

K-002997.check: rg -c prints the existing button count, and cat PLAN.md shows 1rem and 44px.

steps.do: Search index.html and styles.css for existing aria-live attributes.
Search index.html and styles.css for existing role=alert attributes.
Search index.html and styles.css for existing role=status attributes.
Count existing toast-related selectors so you do not duplicate a container.
Decide error toasts use role=alert and success toasts use role=status.
