K-003099.example: At 320px the three toasts have vertical boxes at y 16, 92, and 168, each 64px tall, so no pair intersects and the count is 3. If the second toast starts at y 40 instead, the overlap assertion fails.
K-003099.check: Playwright prints '1 passed', and the test log shows toast count 3 with zero overlapping pairs.
traps: Checking only the first toast and assuming the rest stack correctly.
Using a fixed pixel top offset that overlaps when the viewport height is short.
Triggering the toasts too fast so the count assertion races with the removal timer.

steps.do: Build the production bundle so Lighthouse tests the real output.
Start the preview server in its own terminal and leave it running.
Run Lighthouse on the toast demo route, limited to the accessibility category, and write the JSON report.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report.

K-003100.example: The report prints 0.96 for the accessibility score, which is above the 0.90 threshold. If it prints 0.78, the audit flags missing button names on the toast dismiss control.
K-003100.check: jq prints a number of 0.90 or higher, and the lh-toast.json file exists in the working directory.
traps: Auditing the dev server instead of the built preview, which can give different results.
Reading the performance score when the accessibility score is the one that matters here.
Forgetting that Lighthouse defaults to mobile emulation, so a desktop-only result is not valid evidence.

steps.do: Find the toast color variables in the stylesheet.
Run axe against the toast demo route limited to WCAG 2.0 AA rules.
Confirm the report lists no color-contrast violations for the toast elements.
Confirm the success and error toast colors each give at least 4.5:1 against their background.

K-003101.example: A toast with text #1f2937 on background #ffffff gives a ratio of about 15.8:1, which passes. A light gray #9ca3af on white gives about 2.5:1, which fails and must be darkened.
K-003101.check: The axe run exits with code 0 and reports 0 color-contrast violations for the toast selector.
traps: Checking only the default theme and missing the dark-mode toast colors.
Testing the close icon color and skipping the toast message text.
Treating a 3:1 ratio as enough, when normal-size text needs 4.5:1.

steps.do: Confirm the toast uses a Svelte transition such as fly or fade from svelte/transition.
Confirm the global stylesheet has a prefers-reduced-motion media query.
Run the motion spec with reduced motion emulated and with normal motion.
Confirm the spec asserts the entry transition duration is at most 200ms under normal motion.
Confirm the spec asserts the transition duration is 0ms when reduced motion is set.

K-003102.example: With normal motion the fly transition uses duration 180 and finishes within 200ms, which passes. With reducedMotion set to reduce the toast appears with duration 0, which also passes.
K-003102.check: Playwright prints '2 passed', one for each motion setting.
traps: Using a transition duration above 200ms because it looks smooth in a demo.
Skipping the reduced-motion media query, so users who opt out still see the animation.
Testing transitions in jsdom, which does not run CSS animations, so the duration check proves nothing.

steps.do: Start the Vite dev server in one terminal and leave it running.
Confirm the dev server answers on port 5173.
Run the mobile Playwright spec that sets the viewport to 375px wide.
Confirm the spec reads the computed grid track count instead of counting li elements.

K-003103.example: The spec calls page.setViewportSize with width 375 and height 812, then checks that the ul with role list has one grid track. The same spec expects three tracks at width 1280.
K-003103.check: Playwright prints a line like '2 passed' and exits with code 0, and the rg step prints at least one line containing gridTemplateColumns.
traps: A small model often tests only at the default desktop width and never sets a phone viewport.
Counting li elements proves nothing about layout, so read the computed CSS instead.

steps.do: Run the overflow Playwright spec that compares page width to viewport width at 360px.
Run the measurement script that prints scrollWidth and clientWidth for the products page at 360px.
Check that the printed scrollWidth equals clientWidth, and fix the CSS if it does not.

K-003104.example: At 360px the script prints scrollWidth 360 and clientWidth 360, so the page has no sideways scroll. A product name of 80 unbroken characters would print scrollWidth 412 and fail the spec.
K-003104.check: The script prints scrollWidth=360 clientWidth=360 and the Playwright spec reports passed with exit code 0.
traps: A small model may compare against window.innerWidth instead of document.documentElement.clientWidth.
Setting overflow hidden hides the bug instead of fixing it, so the spec should still fail after such a change.

steps.do: Start the dev server if it is not already running.
Run axe with the WCAG 2.2 tag against the products page.
Run the touch-target Playwright spec that reads each row button boundingBox at 375px.
Confirm the spec defines the minimum height constant as 44.

K-003105.example: Each row button measures at least 44px tall at 375px wide, and the axe run lists no target-size violations for the list.
K-003105.check: Axe lists no target-size violations, Playwright reports passed, and the rg step shows a line with minHeight and the value 44.
traps: Target size applies to the clickable element box, not the icon inside it, so measure the button.
Small models often measure the svg and report a false pass.

steps.do: Install dependencies if the node_modules folder is missing.
Run the component test that mocks window.matchMedia for both narrow and wide widths.
Confirm the test file mocks matchMedia with matches set to true and to false.
Run the TypeScript compiler to confirm the hook types still check.

K-003106.example: With matches set to true the test expects the ul to carry data-columns 1, and with matches set to false it expects data-columns 3.
K-003106.check: Vitest prints 1 test file passed, the rg step shows two matchMedia mocks, and tsc prints nothing with exit code 0.
traps: jsdom does not implement window.matchMedia, so the test crashes unless it is mocked.
A small model often mocks only the true case and forgets the false case, and this test does not prove real layout, so keep the Playwright check too.

steps.do: Build the app so the audit measures optimized production code.
Create the reports folder for the audit output.
Serve the built app on port 4173 in its own terminal and leave it running.
Run Lighthouse with 360px mobile emulation and save the result as JSON.
Read the performance score from the saved report.

K-003107.example: The list page at 360px reports a performance score of 0.92 and an accessibility score of 1.00, both at or above the 0.9 target.
K-003107.check: The jq command prints a number of 0.9 or higher, and the accessibility score in the same file is 1 or close to 1.
traps: Auditing the dev server gives misleading numbers, so audit the preview build.
A small model often starts the preview server in the same shell and then gets connection refused from Lighthouse.

steps.do: Count the media rules in the list CSS module.
List each media rule with its line number.
Check that the breakpoints are min-width 640px and min-width 1024px.
Check that the CSS module is formatted with the project rules.

K-003108.example: The count step prints 2, and the min-width step shows lines for 640px and 1024px with no max-width rules.
K-003108.check: rg -c prints 2, the min-width lines show 640px and 1024px, and prettier reports the file as formatted with exit code 0.
traps: rg -c counts matching lines, so one media block with two conditions counts once.
Small models often add max-width queries, which break the mobile-first order used by min-width.

steps.do: Start a static server for the demo page on port 8080.
Install Playwright and the axe adapter as dev dependencies.
Run the spec that emulates colorScheme light and then dark.
Confirm the axe color-contrast rule reports zero violations in each run, with 4.5:1 as the minimum for normal text.

K-003109.example: In light mode #1a1a1a text on #ffffff is 17.4:1, and in dark mode #f9fafb on #1f2937 is 14.0:1, both above 4.5:1. A failing run prints 'expected 0 violations, received 1' with color-contrast in the rule id.
K-003109.check: Output ends with '2 passed' and no line names the color-contrast rule.
traps: Running the spec once tests only light mode.
Skipping colorScheme emulation leaves the dark branch unchecked.

steps.do: Confirm the stylesheet declares a forced-colors media query.
Confirm the media block uses the CanvasText system color for the outline.
Run the spec that sets forcedColors to active and reads computed outline and border values.
Confirm the toast keeps a visible border or outline with a width of at least 2px under forced colors.

K-003110.example: The media block sets outline: 2px solid CanvasText, and the computed outline-width reads 2px. Under forced colors the computed border-top-style must be solid, not none.
K-003110.check: The grep prints an '@media (forced-colors: active)' line, and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Forced colors strips background-color and box-shadow, so a shadow-only toast disappears.
Hardcoding a color in the media query ignores the user's system palette.

steps.do: Find the transition declarations in the toast stylesheet.
Confirm a prefers-reduced-motion block exists in the stylesheet.
Run the spec that measures computed transition-duration with and without reduced motion.
Confirm the normal duration is 200ms or less and the reduced-motion duration is 0s.

K-003111.example: The toast rule sets transition: transform 200ms ease, and the reduced-motion block sets transition-duration: 0s. A value of 0.25s fails the spec with 'expected <= 0.2s, received 0.25s'.
K-003111.check: Computed transition-duration reads 0.2s normally and 0s under reduced motion, and Playwright prints '2 passed'.
traps: Reading the CSS text alone misses overrides from other selectors.
Forgetting to emulate reducedMotion as reduce leaves the reduced branch untested.

steps.do: Confirm the dark demo page exists before auditing it.
Run Lighthouse on the dark page for the accessibility category only.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report.
Confirm the score is 0.95 or higher, and fix any failed audit the report names.

K-003112.example: Lighthouse reports an accessibility score of 1 on toast-dark.html, which sets data-theme to dark on the html element. A score of 0.87 means a failed audit such as color-contrast, which the report lists under failed audits.
K-003112.check: The test command exits 0 with no output, and jq prints 1 or a value of at least 0.95.
traps: Auditing only the dark page misses light-mode regressions.
Omitting --output-path leaves jq with no file to read.

steps.do: Count toast nodes marked as live regions in the demo page.
Run the spec that opens three toasts, sets data-theme to dark, and reads background-color.
Confirm the spec asserts the background changes from rgb(255, 255, 255) to rgb(31, 41, 55) within 200ms.
Confirm the spec reads the restyled background without calling page.reload.

K-003113.example: Setting document.documentElement.dataset.theme to dark turns the three open toasts from rgb(255, 255, 255) to rgb(31, 41, 55). A failing run prints 'expected rgb(31, 41, 55), received rgb(255, 255, 255)' when the toggle misses an open toast.
K-003113.check: The grep prints 3, and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Testing only newly created toasts misses ones already mounted.
Calling reload makes the restyle look passing even when no live update happened.

steps.do: List the styles directory to confirm styles/toast.css exists before counting.
Count lines with hex color literals in styles/toast.css. The printed number must be exactly 8, all inside the :root and [data-theme='dark'] token blocks.
Count lines that read a theme token through var(--toast-) in styles/toast.css. The printed number must be 6 or more.
Confirm no !important declarations override a theme value. The grep must print nothing and exit with status 1.

K-003114.example: The hex count prints 8 for toast.css, all inside the :root and [data-theme='dark'] token blocks with 4 each. The var(--toast- count prints 9, and the !important grep prints nothing.
K-003114.check: The hex count prints exactly 8, the var count is 6 or more, and the !important grep prints nothing with exit status 1.
traps: Counting hex across the whole project mixes in unrelated files.
An empty grep result means no matches, which is a pass here, not an error.

steps.do: Find existing searchable lists and their current empty branches.
Plan ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) for a non-empty query that returns no rows.
Plan a ContentUnavailableView with a title and systemImage for the no-data case.
Plan to render only one empty view per state, never both at once.
Verify each file in the views folder uses at most 2 ContentUnavailableView.

K-003115.example: InboxView shows ContentUnavailableView.search(text: query) when the query is not empty, and ContentUnavailableView('No messages', systemImage: 'tray') when the inbox is empty. The rg count shows 2 for InboxView.swift and no file above 2.
K-003115.check: rg -c prints 2 or fewer for every file, matching the planned count.
traps: Small models show one generic message for both cases, which hides why results are missing.
Putting both empty views in one ZStack adds layout work with no visible benefit.

steps.do: List every padding call in the sources with its value.
Count how many padding calls use a literal number instead of a token.
Write a spacing scale in the plan with steps of 4pt, 8pt, 16pt, 24pt, and 32pt.

K-003116.example: A call padding(13) is off the grid and should map to padding(.medium) or 12pt, while padding(16) already fits the scale. The plan sets spacing tokens xs at 4pt, sm at 8pt, and md at 16pt.
K-003116.check: rg -n lists each padding value, and every value in the plan's scale is a multiple of 4.
traps: Do not invent a new spacing value for each screen; reuse the scale so spacing stays consistent.
Padding values in previews count too, so decide whether to include them before counting.

steps.do: List every frame modifier and its size arguments in the sources.
Find buttons whose labels lack a minimum size modifier.
Write a plan rule that every tappable text element has a minimum height of 44pt.

K-003117.example: A Button with the label Text("Save") and .frame(minHeight: 44) passes the rule, while an unframed label of 17pt text at about 22pt tall fails. The plan adds a ButtonStyle that applies the minimum height to every button.
K-003117.check: rg -n shows that each Button in the plan lists a frame with minHeight of at least 44, and no tappable label is listed without one.
traps: Text height alone is not the tap target, so the frame must set minHeight rather than rely on the font size.
Do not reduce the minimum to 32pt to fit a dense layout, because the accessibility guideline requires 44pt.

steps.do: List the color definitions already present in the design system folder.
Check the asset catalog for named color sets that the tokens will reference.
With the app preview already running on localhost port 8080, run the axe runner against it for the WCAG AA color-contrast rule.

K-003118.example: A body text token on a background token must reach 4.5:1, so a pair measuring 4.7:1 passes, while a pair at 3.9:1 fails. Large text at 18pt regular or 14pt bold needs only 3:1.
K-003118.check: axe reports zero color-contrast violations at wcag2aa, which means every body text pair reaches 4.5:1 and every large text pair reaches 3:1.
traps: A color that looks clear on a light screen can fail the 4.5:1 ratio, so run the runner rather than judge by eye.
Do not hardcode Color(red:green:blue:) values in views; reference the named token instead.

steps.do: Create the styles directory for the design tokens.
Create an empty tokens file.
Declare --font-size-sm 0.875rem, --font-size-base 1rem, --font-size-lg 1.25rem and --font-size-xl 1.5rem inside a :root block in tokens.css.
Add an @import line for tokens.css at the top of the main stylesheet.
Count the font-size token declarations, expecting four.
List any literal px font sizes left in components, expecting none.

K-003119.example: tokens.css declares --font-size-base: 1rem at :root, and the button rule uses font-size: var(--font-size-base) instead of 16px. Rem keeps the base size tied to the user's browser default.
K-003119.check: grep -c prints 4, and rg prints no lines and exits with code 1.
traps: Writing 16px instead of 1rem breaks user zoom.
Declaring tokens on a component instead of :root makes them unavailable elsewhere.
Forgetting var() around the name applies the literal text instead of the value.

steps.do: Open the tokens stylesheet to find where the heading tokens belong.
Add --font-size-h1 with clamp(1.75rem, 1.2rem + 2.5vw, 3rem) inside :root.
Add --font-size-h2 with clamp(1.375rem, 1.1rem + 1.2vw, 2rem) inside :root.
Apply var(--font-size-h1) to the h1 rule in the page stylesheet.
Count the clamp declarations, expecting two.
Write a Playwright test asserting the h1 computed font size is 28px at a 320px viewport and 48px at a 1280px viewport, then run it.

K-003120.example: At 320px the h1 computes to 28px and at 1280px it computes to 48px, because clamp keeps the middle value between 1.75rem and 3rem. The vw term makes the size grow with the viewport width between those limits.
K-003120.check: rg prints 2 and Playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: Using only vw with no rem term makes text ignore the user's browser font size.
Swapping the min and max values gives an inverted range.
Testing without setting the viewport width makes the 28px and 48px checks meaningless.

steps.do: Create the color tokens file.
Declare raw values --palette-gray-900 #1a1a1a and --palette-white #ffffff inside :root.
Declare --color-text as var(--palette-gray-900) and --color-surface as var(--palette-white) inside :root.
Override only --color-text and --color-surface inside a [data-theme=dark] selector.
Count the --color- declarations, expecting four: two in :root and two in the dark theme.
Run axe against the running page and confirm the text and surface pair meets 4.5:1 contrast.

K-003121.example: --color-text resolves to #1a1a1a and --color-surface to #ffffff, a contrast ratio of 17.4:1. The dark theme swaps only those two aliases, so components never change their rules.
K-003121.check: grep -c prints 4 and axe reports zero color-contrast violations.
traps: Referencing palette names inside components bypasses the theme.
Putting the dark override on :root instead of the data-theme selector breaks the cascade order.
Writing a hex value in a semantic alias skips the palette.

steps.do: Create the fonts directory.
Copy the vendored variable font file into the fonts directory.
Declare an @font-face rule for Inter with a src url to the woff2 file, font-weight 100 900, and font-display swap.
Add a preload link in the head for the woff2 file with type font/woff2 and the crossorigin attribute.
Check the font file size, expecting fewer than 102400 bytes.
Run Lighthouse and confirm the font-display audit passes.

K-003122.example: Inter-Var.woff2 is 98304 bytes, under the 100 KB budget. font-display: swap shows the fallback sans-serif immediately while Inter loads.
K-003122.check: stat prints a number below 102400 and the Lighthouse font-display audit passes.
traps: Omitting the font-weight range makes the variable axis unusable.
Leaving crossorigin off the preload makes the browser fetch the font twice.
Linking a third-party font URL instead of the vendored file adds an extra request.

steps.do: List every literal px font-size in the components directory.
For each match, replace the value with the matching token such as var(--font-size-base).
Count the font-size declarations in the components directory to record the baseline.
Recheck for literal px font sizes after the edits, expecting no output.
Run stylelint on the component stylesheets to catch regressions.

K-003123.example: button.css line 4 changes font-size: 14px to font-size: var(--font-size-sm), so the button follows the 0.875rem token. After the edit, rg finds no literal px font sizes in the components directory.
K-003123.check: The final rg search prints zero lines and stylelint exits with code 0.
traps: Using var() with an undefined token name silently falls back to the initial value.
Converting 14px to 0.875rem by hand duplicates a value that already has a token.
Editing only the first match in a file misses repeated declarations.

steps.do: Confirm the installed React version.
Find files whose names contain form.
Count the input elements in the form component.
Write the React version and the field count into the plan.

K-003124.example: npm ls react prints react@18.3.1, and grep -c input prints 6, so the plan covers 6 fields on React 18. The plan records both values before any layout is chosen.
K-003124.check: npm ls react prints a line such as react@18.3.1, and grep prints a number such as 6, both written into the plan.
traps: Assuming React 19 APIs exist without checking the installed version.
Counting only type="text" inputs and missing select, textarea, and fieldset elements.

steps.do: List the existing media query lines in the source.
Check whether a matchMedia based hook already exists.
Confirm the planned stylesheet path is still free.
Record the breakpoints in the plan: 0 to 639px one column, 640px and up two columns, 1024px and up three columns.

K-003125.example: grep -rn @media src shows a rule at 768px in src/index.css, so the plan uses 640px and 1024px and avoids that value. test -f exits with status 1 because the CSS module does not exist yet.
K-003125.check: grep lists each existing width, and test -f exits with status 1, meaning the file is new.
traps: Choosing breakpoints that duplicate existing ones with different values.
Reading test -f output as text, when it reports presence only through its exit status.

steps.do: Find existing height rules that could conflict with the new targets.
List the CSS files that the form styles would sit beside.
Read the project scripts to see how the CSS will be checked later.
Record in the plan: inputs and buttons get min-height 44px and font-size 1rem so iOS does not zoom on focus.

K-003126.example: grep -rn height src finds height: 32px in src/index.css, so the form module must override it for inputs and buttons. The plan sets min-height: 44px and font-size: 1rem, which is 16px at the default root size.
K-003126.check: grep reports the old height lines, and the plan names 44px as the minimum for every input and button.
traps: Setting 44px only on the submit button and forgetting the text inputs.
Using px for font-size when the plan states 1rem.

steps.do: Count the name attributes in the form to estimate the number of fields.
Check for existing grid-template-columns rules to reuse.
List the components directory to confirm where the form lives.
Record in the plan: one column below 640px, two columns from 640px, with first name and last name paired.

K-003127.example: grep -c name= prints 4, so the plan pairs 4 fields into 2 rows at 640px and above. Below 640px all fields stack in one column with a gap of 1rem.
K-003127.check: grep prints a count of 4, and the plan lists two rows of paired fields with a 640px breakpoint.
traps: Using a grid with fixed column widths that overflows at 320px.
Counting name= matches that appear in more than one file.

steps.do: Check whether useId is already used in the source.
Confirm the React version supports useId, which needs React 18 or later.
Count the label elements in the form to match them against the fields.
Record in the plan: each error span gets an id from useId, and its input sets aria-describedby to that id.

K-003128.example: The plan gives the email field an id from useId and sets aria-describedby to the error span, so the 2 fields with errors each keep their link at 320px. grep -c "<label" should print 6 to match the 6 fields.
K-003128.check: grep -c prints a count equal to the number of fields, and npm ls react shows version 18 or higher.
traps: Hard-coding ids such as email-error, which collide when the form renders twice.
Passing the useId value to querySelector, where its colons break the selector.

steps.do: List the physical horizontal utilities still in the card.
steps.cmd: grep -n -e pl- -e pr- -e ml- -e mr- -e text-left -e text-right src/components/Card.tsx

steps.do: Replace each pl- with ps-, each pr- with pe-, each ml- with ms-, and each mr- with me-.
Replace text-left with text-start and text-right with text-end.
Confirm no physical horizontal utilities remain in the card.
steps.cmd: grep -c -e pl- -e pr- -e ml- -e mr- -e text-left -e text-right src/components/Card.tsx

steps.do: Set dir to rtl on the test page root and run the RTL layout test.

K-003129.example: A card with class 'pl-4 pr-6 text-left' becomes 'ps-4 pe-6 text-start'. The Playwright test asserts the title's right edge sits within 4px of the card's right edge when dir is rtl.
K-003129.check: The grep -c command prints 0 and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models keep pl- because it looks equivalent in LTR, but it does not flip under RTL. Do not mix ps- with pl- on the same element. Use text-start and text-end, not text-left and text-right.

steps.do: Find the chevron or arrow icon element in the card.
Add rtl:-scale-x-100 to that icon's className.
Count the rtl: variants now in the card.
Build the stylesheet so the variant compiles.
Check the compiled CSS contains a dir=rtl selector.
Run the icon direction test.

K-003130.example: <ChevronRight className='size-4 rtl:-scale-x-100' /> points left when dir is rtl. The compiled CSS contains a rule that matches [dir=rtl] and the grep count is 1 or more.
K-003130.check: grep -c rtl dist/output.css prints 1 or more and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models use rotate-180 for direction, which also flips the icon vertically. Set dir on html or a wrapper, not on each card. Use rtl:-scale-x-100 so only the horizontal axis flips.

steps.do: Find the title and label elements in the card.
Add min-w-0 to the flex child that holds the title.
Add break-words and line-clamp-2 to the title element.
Create a test fixture with a title about 40 percent longer than the English string.
Count the overflow classes now in the card.
Run the overflow test that asserts no horizontal scroll.

K-003131.example: A 41-character German title wraps to two lines under line-clamp-2, and the test asserts scrollWidth is less than or equal to clientWidth. The grep count prints 3 when all three classes are present.
K-003131.check: grep -c prints 3 or more and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models add truncate, which hides translated text instead of wrapping it. Do not set a fixed height such as h-12, since longer strings need more lines.

steps.do: Find the body text element in the card.
Add the arbitrary variant [:lang(ja)]:leading-loose to the body element.
Add the arbitrary variant [:lang(zh)]:leading-loose to the same element.
Check the html element declares a lang attribute.
Run the typography test that reads the computed line height.

K-003132.example: A paragraph with text-base and [:lang(ja)]:leading-loose gets a 32px line height on Japanese text at a 16px font size. The test asserts getComputedStyle(p).lineHeight equals 32px.
K-003132.check: grep prints the lang line and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models put lang only on the card instead of the html element, which breaks the variant for the rest of the page. Do not apply leading-loose to Latin text when only Japanese and Chinese need it.

steps.do: Find the border and rounded utilities on the card root.
Replace border-l-4 with border-s-4.
Replace rounded-l-xl with rounded-s-xl.
Replace border-l-blue-500 with border-s-blue-500.
Confirm no physical left-side border or rounded utilities remain.
Run the accent bar test in RTL.

K-003133.example: A card with class 'border-s-4 border-s-blue-500 rounded-s-xl' shows the blue bar on the right edge when dir is rtl. The test asserts the bar's boundingBox().x is greater than the card's horizontal midpoint.
K-003133.check: grep -c prints 0 and Playwright prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models keep border-l next to border-s, so both sides get styled. Use border-s-4 with border-s-{color}, since border-s alone sets only the width.

steps.do: List the hardcoded user-visible text in the card.
steps.cmd: grep -n -e Title -e Label -e Button -e Read src/components/Card.tsx

steps.do: Replace each literal with a t call keyed by the card namespace, such as t('card.readMore').
Add the key card.readMore with the English value Read more to locales/en/common.json.
Add the key card.readMore with the German value Mehr lesen to locales/de/common.json.
Count the card keys in the English locale file. Expect 2 for this card.
Count the card keys in the German locale file. Expect the same number as the English file.
Run the key parity test and confirm it reports 1 passed.

K-003134.example: Replace the literal 'Read more' with {t('card.readMore')} and add the German value 'Mehr lesen' under the same key. Both locale files then report the same count of card. keys.
K-003134.check: Both grep counts print 2 for this card, and the parity test prints '1 passed' after npx playwright test tests/card-i18n.spec.ts runs.
traps: Small models translate the value inside the component instead of the locale file. Use the same key names in every locale, or a missing key will render as the raw key string.

steps.do: Start the dev server on a fixed port so the test run has a known URL.
Run the Playwright spec that emulates a dark color scheme and reads the table background.
Confirm the spec expects the tbody background to be rgb(18, 18, 20) in dark mode.
